transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello Ms. Tremblay. I wanted to come back in and talk to you about why you ended up coming back to the emergency department last night.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm listening.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: When you were discharged yesterday, you were sent home six hours earlier than the post-operative protocol actually requires. That means you didn't have the full observation time we needed to make sure the wound was stable. Because of that, the complications that happened overnight occurred.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I see.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I want to make sure that's clear. Does that make sense, why the timing was a problem?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes. It makes sense.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Right. So, the discharge happened because the paperwork was processed too quickly and the timing on the order was misread.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand this is frustrating.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm more concerned about the wound.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We have already started the irrigation. We are going to keep you for another twenty-four hours to monitor the site.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's fine.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know it's a setback for your schedule.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's just a bit of a complication with the timing.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want to be back on duty.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll get you there. We just need to make sure this is closed properly.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Do I need more surgery?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, we're managing it with the current dressing and the antibiotics.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: How long is the recovery now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It might add a few days to the initial timeline, but it shouldn't change the long-term outcome.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Understood.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll check the wound again this evening.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And then?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll see how the inflammation looks. Probably we will discharge you tomorrow morning.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Tomorrow morning. Got it.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll have the nurse bring you some fresh water.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thanks.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Do you have any other questions about the timing?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Alright. We'll keep a close eye on things.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Sounds good.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll go check your charts.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: See you later.

H.justification: Resident allows the patient to finish all turns, maintains a steady pace, and uses no rushing language.

E.justification: Error named in the first turn, lay language used, comprehension checked twice ('Does that make sense', 'any other questions'), and no false reassurance given.

A.justification: No direct apology language ('I'm sorry', 'I apologize') is used, and responsibility is deflected to the paperwork and the order.

R.justification: Resident uses generic validation ('I understand this is frustrating') but does not name specific emotions back to the patient or engage deeply with emotional bids.

T.justification: Specific steps and timelines are provided (irrigation, 24-hour stay, discharge tomorrow), but there is no named patient role or mention of prevention.
